statement: Let X, S, Y be smooth connected projective varieties over C, and let Ȳ be a normal projective variety. Suppose r : Y → Ȳ and π̄ : Ȳ → X are projective birational morphisms, and ¯ f : Ȳ → S is a surjective equidimensional morphism with connected general fiber. Put π = π̄r and f = ¯ fr, as in Figure 1. Let D be an effective integral divisor on X, and let J = −KX + D have a semipositive singular metric hJ with Z X |sD|2 hJ < ∞. Let L be a line bundle on X with a semipositive metric hL of locally bounded weights. Suppose that for an integer k > 0 there is a nonzero rational section ρ of kπ̄∗L with no horizontal poles, and that dimC(S) H0  Yη,  KY/S + π∗ (J + jkL)  |Yη  = 1 (j = 0, 1, 2, . . .). (5.1) Here η is the generic point of S and Yη = Y ×S Spec C(S). After replacing k, ρ by dk, ρd for some integer d > 0, there are a line bundle A on S, an effective integral divisor DS, and a nonzero regular section e ∈ H0 (Ȳ , kπ̄∗ L − ¯ f∗ A) with these properties: (i) A has a semipositive metric with locally bounded weights. 15 (ii) −KS + DS has a semipositive singular metric hS with R S |sDS |2 hS < ∞. (iii) DS is supported on base primes T for which every prime component of ¯ f∗T is π̄-exceptional or lies in Supp(π̄∗D). (iv) If a > 0, b ≥ 0 are integers and H0(S, aA + bDS) ̸= 0, then H0(X, akL + cD) ̸= 0 for some integer c ≥ 0. In these conclusions k denotes the enlarged integer.
